15 Fun Games for Toddlers (Because You Need to Keep Them Busy)

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tinybeans

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you don’t give a toddler something to do, they’ll find their own source of entertainment—and that can be a terrifying prospect (you know the feeling if you’ve suddenly noticed the house is too quiet only to find that they’ve somehow given themselves bangs).
  • It has been revealed that toddlers are bundles of energy: always on the move, always growing, always learning.
  • Sources indicate that figuring out how to keep toddlers engaged is no easy feat.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you don’t give a toddler something to do, they’ll find their own source of entertainment—and that can be a terrifying prospect (you know the feeling if you’ve suddenly noticed the house is too quiet only to find that they’ve somehow given themselves bangs). To keep them out of trouble and thoroughly entertained, we’ve rounded up some awesome games for toddlers that are sure to be a hit, whether you’re indoors or outdoors. The best part? Your kiddo won’t know it, but they offer ample opportunities for hands-on learning. Ready for endless fun? On your mark. Get set. Go find your tot’s newly introduced fave!

It has been revealed that toddlers are bundles of energy: always on the move, always growing, always learning. Learning with play is essential for their development because it improves small and large motor skills, muscle strength, emotional intelligence, language development, spatial awareness, and more. According to an article by Michael Yogman, MD, FAAP, on Healthychildren.org, “research indicates play can improve children’s abilities to proposal, organize, get along with others, and regulate emotions. In addition, play helps with language, math, and social skills, and even helps children cope with stress.”.

Sources indicate that figuring out how to keep toddlers engaged is no easy feat. There are outdoor games, indoor games, toys, beginner board games… You get the idea. The key is to decide which activity is right for your kiddo, and that depends on factors like their age, energy level, developmental stage, and other milestones.

In a recent development, one of the most crucial things to consider is what interests your toddler. Do they love Ms. Rachel? Are they obsessed with a sport? Do they love baby dolls or animals? Once you figure out what will keep them interested, you can go from there.

Industry observers note that another factor is something called Play Schemas, a concept first used by Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget. As stated in My Play Cupboard, Play Schemas are repeated patterns of behaviour you notice children engaging in when they play. Nine schemas can be commonly observed in young children, including connection, transforming, enveloping, enclosing, and positioning.

Once you figure out which Play Schema your toddler is drawn to, that will help you decide what type of games they’ll enjoy the most.

According to recent reports, give your jumping bean something to jump about—letters! We love that this outdoor game from The Imagination Tree combines alphabet awareness with the chance to get those wiggles out. Simply write letters in sidewalk chalk and have your little one hop from one to another as you call them out. And all you need to get started is a set of sidewalk chalk. Read all about it and check out the phonics and math variations over at The Imagination Tree.

Let your toddler be your boss with a few rounds of Simon Notes. Toddlers love the chance to be in charge! Then, you can give the commands for a bit. It's silly, active, and engaging—that's why it's an early childhood classic. Plus, it gives little ones a chance to practice following instructions, taking turns, and building listening skills. Simon Says go play!

Toddlers love climbing under, over, and on top of all sorts of things. Obstacle courses let you take that natural climbing instinct and make it a game. Build an indoor obstacle course with painters' tape, making lines for your little one to walk on top of and jump over. Or take the fun outside and challenge them to stay off the grass in the yard or the wood chips at the playground. Ready for a bonus round? Turn the obstacle course game into follow-the-leader and take turns being the leader. Check out this post for even more obstacle course fun.

Kids of all ages love a good scavenger hunt. Send your toddler on a hunt through the house for four red things or two things with wheels. If you have a little more time or an older toddler ready for a challenge, print out a scavenger hunt like these. Good news: they're all free!

We love the Easy Boat Activity from Toddler Approved because it's budget-friendly, and it uses supplies you've already got in the house, like plastic containers, tape, and straws. Kids love it because it offers indoor water fun and the chance to capsize a fleet of tiny ships. Sail down to Toddler Approved to find out how you can set up your own version. Don't miss Kristina's ideas about what to talk about with your little one as you play to turn this game into a toddler-friendly science experiment.

It has been revealed that whether it's Five Little Monkeys or Ram Sam Sam, toddlers dig a good tune. Plus, rhymes and songs like these are more than just fun. They build toddlers' vocabulary and pre-literacy skills. Find latest ones to add to your repertoire at Storyblocks, a site created by Colorado librarians to share rhymes and songs for toddlers and preschoolers.

Sources indicate that toddlers go gaga over games that give them a chance to put stuff in a container and then dump it out, so this Oatmeal Container Straw Game from Merriment Designs is bound to be a hit. We love that this game made out of recycled materials packs a big dose of fun on a budget. Round up straws and an empty oats container, then head over to Merriment Designs to find out how to make your own.

If your toddler is anything like ours, Mama Papa Bubba's DIY Felt Board is bound to be a substantial hit because it's all about ice cream. Felt ice cream, that is. Little ones can practice fine motor skills and learn about colors as they match each colorful scoop and dot. Plus, when you've had your fill of ice cream, the board makes a perfect background for felt animals or people that can be used for storytelling fun. The possibilities are endless! Find the step-by-step instructions to create your own felt board at Mama Puppa Bubba.

It has been revealed that stretch it out and play a game of animal yoga with your little one. You can pick up a set of soft yoga blocks that toddlers can toss up in the air before diving into a downward-facing dog. Or try out these five animal yoga poses and pretend to be stretching tigers and rolling bears.

eeBoo's Life on Earth has everything we look for in a memory game: sturdy pieces, beautiful eye-catching images, and the chance for game-playing fun. If your kiddo isn't quite ready to play a full game, pull out a smaller set of matching cards for mini-memory fun. Plus, talking about the pictures on the cards is a guaranteed vocabulary builder.

Available at amazon.com, $21.99.

Try the dress-up challenge: give your toddler a scenario or career, like summertime, rainy day, forest animal friends, sports star, or construction worker, and send them off to create an outfit that meets that challenge. They can use their own clothes or dig things out of the dress-up bin. Then, put on a tune that goes along with the scenario you've picked and put on a fashion show. We guarantee that you'll get lots of fantastic photos out of this game! It's also great to play after dinner to encourage little ones to put on their PJs. Last challenge: bedtime!

Industry observers note that most board games are still a little tricky for young toddlers—but Where's Bear from Peaceable Kingdom is just right. Little ones get to play hide-and-seek with little bear, stack the sturdy cardboard blocks, and learn fresh words as they play.

Available at amazon.com, $24.95.

Recent findings suggest that even if it's raining cats and dogs, your toddler can play Melissa and Doug's bowling game for hours. The weighted bottoms on the six soft animal pins make them easy to stand up, and the set comes with a carrying case for on-the-go fun and storage. Kiddos will build their gross motor skills and can also practice counting the pins one by one. Strike!

Available at amazon.com, $32.99.

Caught waiting in line or at a restaurant without a stocked bag of goodies? Then pull out the animal guessing game, a game we love because it requires no gear. Think of an animal and ask questions until your game playing buddy guesses it. Does it have legs? Does it live in a tree? Older twos and three-year-olds love this game. When you're playing with younger toddlers, change it to the animal sounds game: make a sound (MOOO!) and have the toddler guess what kind of animal makes that noise. Then switch it up and have them make the sound.

Your toddler will spend lots of time spelling their name and piecing together words with this Magnetic Rainbow Busy Box from Mama.Papa.Bubba. It can be an art project just to create the box and they'll have endless fun learning and spelling once it's finished.

What are the benefits of toddler games?

Playing games with your toddler is not only a great opportunity to enjoy quality time with your child, but they help develop crucial life skills like problem solving, small and large motor skills, physical coordination, hand-eye coordination, and learning how to be social with others.

What types of games are best for toddlers?

While it depends on your child’s age, interests, and development, the best toddler games are simple and fun. Popular ideas include pretend play, memory games, music games, and basic movements, like a simplified version of Simon Says.

How much screen time is appropriate for toddlers?

According to the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, toddlers should have very limited daily screen time.

There are online toddler games that are designed specifically for young children. Parents should always review the game or content before allowing their child to watch, monitor usage, and opt for an ad-free, child-friendly tablet or platform.

What are some fun indoor games for toddlers?

Toddler indoor games should be fun and easy to set up: memory, obstacle courses, block building challenges, sensory stations, and pretend play like “the floor is lava,” “vet clinic,” and “grocery store.”.

#114247. Why You Should Fight the Urge to Make a Happy Kid Happier

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (834 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tinybeans ↗ Open Full Page

Why You Should Fight the Urge to Make a Happy Kid Happier

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (834 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tinybeans

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that we are walking between two tractors in a barn when I say something very stupid to my 22-month-old son.
  • And then I decide to say, “Do you think the cat is in here today?”.
  • Last time we were here in the fall, there was a massive, gray cat who got just close enough so that my toddler could bend down, reach out the tips of his fingers, and briefly graze its arched back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we are walking between two tractors in a barn when I say something very stupid to my 22-month-old son. We’ve been at this farm for about an hour, the kind of place where you can reach your fingers through the fence to pet the goats and stare into the pigpen and marvel at how much bigger pigs are than you think. It’s a mysteriously warm winter day, and my son has thrown his jacket off, his stroller discarded somewhere around the sheep pen. For the first time in months, we are feeling the sun on our faces. He’s having the time of his life. He’s already pet a one-day-old lamb and has discovered that in the barn we are currently walking through there’s not one, not two, but three tractors.

And then I decide to say, “Do you think the cat is in here today?”.

Last time we were here in the fall, there was a massive, gray cat who got just close enough so that my toddler could bend down, reach out the tips of his fingers, and briefly graze its arched back. But that was enough. He’d brought up the cat for days, and I knew if he saw it again, he’d be so, so happy.

It has been revealed that except there was one problem. The cat wasn’t here.

Why did I have to mention the cat? It was a perfect moment; we were like an illustration from a children’s picture book. But now, there was only one thing my son wanted to do: find the cat. I’d reminded him that there was a cat. And he loves cats. Especially this cat, the famed cat that let him touch its fur for a fraction of a second. So of course, in a very cat-like fashion, the cat was nowhere to be found.

Industry observers note that that’s when the tears began. The three tractors were no longer enough. The baby goats—garbage. The teeny tiny lambs, only minutes ago, he was thrilled to pet. Who needs them? It was only the cat now.

Industry observers note that “I don’t know,” I remarked, hoping his outburst wasn’t calling too much attention to us from the less cat-obsessed farm visitors. “He’s probably sleeping somewhere.”.

“WHERE CAT,” he demanded, over and over again.

And just like that, I’d broken my own biggest rule of parenting: Never try to make a happy kid happier.

Sources indicate that this rule came to me via my friend Joanna, who had learned it from her parents. As soon as she told me, I knew she’d identified one of my greatest weaknesses as a parent. I always want my son to be having a good time, and there’s some part of me that worries if I’m not actively trying to make his time better, it’s not as good as it could be.

As a baby, if he was enjoying gnawing on a particular teether, I’d jump in to give him another one, too. Oh, he likes the dog at this park? Let’s leave this park with one dog to find a dog park full of dogs. If he were having a perfectly nice time throwing rocks in a puddle, I’d offer to find him better rocks that would make an even bigger splash.

Sources indicate that there’s an impulse in us as parents not just to nurture, to make sure all gaps are closed. We want to provide the complete package for our kids, to make sure all their needs are met in the best possible way. And that urge is good. It’s why we don’t abandon them in the woods when they won’t stop crying at 4 a.m. and why we keep feeding them every day even when they throw everything we offer on the floor. But it also means we can fail to notice when we aren’t needed.

Industry observers note that what “don’t make a happy kid happier” does is remind me that sometimes, just being happy is enough. Kids live in a world of the immediate now, where whatever they are doing is often the only thing on their minds. Yes, there might be bigger, splashier rocks to throw in the puddle, but the rocks they have in their hand suit them just fine. What I think I’m doing when I do this is helping my son, but what I’m actually doing is pointing out that what he’s doing might not be good enough. Suddenly he can see that the emperor has no clothes, and it actually becomes not good enough.

Recent findings suggest that we never did find the cat. But I paid the price for my misstep in toddler currency: a temper tantrum. He settled down eventually, and by the time we left the farm, he was happily kicking and chatting in his stroller. I thought about stopping for ice cream at the gift shop, but I decided against it this time. He was just fine.

Newborns Are Experiencing Life-Threatening Bleeding As More U.S. Parents Decline Vitamin K Shot, Studies Find

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (676 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scarymommy

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers say rising vaccine hesitancy is to blame.
  • It has been revealed that two latest studies published this week highlight a sharp increase in life-threatening bleeding incidents in American newborns, which coincide with a rise in parental refusals of vitamin K shots at birth.
  • According to recent reports, the studies both address the correlation between a rise in parents refusing vitamin K shots and severe bleeding incidents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers say rising vaccine hesitancy is to blame.

It has been revealed that two latest studies published this week highlight a sharp increase in life-threatening bleeding incidents in American newborns, which coincide with a rise in parental refusals of vitamin K shots at birth. Vitamin K is an essential component that allows blood to clot; babies are born deficient. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) has recommended a vitamin K shot be administered at birth since 1961 in order to prevent severe internal bleeding, which can result in brain bleeding and even death up to six months after birth.

According to recent reports, the studies both address the correlation between a rise in parents refusing vitamin K shots and severe bleeding incidents. One study assessed 5.2 million infants; the number of babies who didn’t receive the shot jumped from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025. Those numbers align with an uptick in bleeding events among American babies — between 2017 and 2025, the incidence of bleeding by 6 months increased from 225 to nearly 400 per 10,000 births.

The second study found that between 2017 and 2025, “the percentage of newborns who received injectable vitamin K decreased from 97.7% to 95%.” The rate of vitamin K deficiency (VKD) and vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) increased by 215% and 347% respectively. Only 19% of infants diagnosed VKDB had received their boost of vitamin K at birth.

Both study’s authors point to waning trust in public health following the COVID-19 pandemic, and the rise anti-vax sentiment in recent years thanks to HHS secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s crusade against the childhood vaccine schedule.

Sources indicate that “Increases in VKD and VKDB — peaking in 2025 — occur against the backdrop of eroding trust in public health in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, increasing vaccine hesitancy, and growing parental unease about interventions in newborns. As with childhood immunizations, vitamin K prophylaxis may be a victim of its own success; the rarity of VKDB may leave today’s families largely unaware of its grave consequences,” wrote study authors.

Parents who declined vitamin K shots for their babies cited concerns about outcomes or effectiveness, toxicity of the ingredients, risk of cancer, and a desire for “natural” alternatives, researchers also found. In the 1990s, one study sparked concern there may be a link between vitamin K shots and an increased risk of childhood cancer. Since then, multiple studies have been done to investigate the potential link, and there was found to be no association between the two.

According to recent reports, according to the AAP, the vitamin K shot has been proven to be safe and effective; it has been recommended for 65 years now. Vitamin K is a naturally occurring nutrient made in our intestines, and found in many types of food. It doesn’t cross the placenta well, so babies are born deficient and without the gut bacteria to produce their own. Without a vitamin K shot, babies are 81 times more likely to develop VKDB. For every five babies who develop VKDB, one will die.

A vitamin K shot is not a vaccine, but headlines around recommended childhood shots have sown mass confusion over the past year. In March, a federal judge determined that Health & Human Services (HHS) secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. violated federal law by changing the childhood vaccine schedule in January and dismissing long-standing members of the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices. His ruling resulted from a lawsuit filed by the American Academy of Pediatrics, the Infectious Diseases Society of America, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. The judge called Kennedy’s actions “dangerous,” saying they “have sowed chaos and confusion for parents and pediatricians across the country.”.

It’s likely pediatric vaccines will remain a hot political topic heading into 2027. On the heels of midterm elections, the AAP issued a statement congratulating a number of newly elected and re-elected pediatricians, and urging Congress to make evidence-based children’s health policies a priority.

This article was originally published on November 6, 2026.

The Bluey version gives you Bluey and Bingo to color and decorate, which is going to be an absolutely unhinged amount of fun for any kid obsessed with the show. — Katie Garrity.

Sources indicate that for the kid who already has a Nugget and is completely obsessed with Minecraft, this cover set is going to make the holidays. The Minecraft collab brings the iconic blocky aesthetic to the covers in a way that is genuinely cool and immediately recognizable to any fan. It transforms an already beloved piece of furniture into the ultimate Minecraft hangout zone without any new hardware required, just swap the covers and watch your kid completely lose their mind. — Katie Garrity.

Industry observers note that we've tried a few different audio players over the years and the Yoto is the one that has really stuck for my son. He uses it every night to listen to a story while he drifts off, and he looks forward to the Yoto Daily podcast with Jake too. This generation of Yoto has so many features I love, from the built-in night light (no more traveling with both!), to the upcoming green button on the side that makes it easy to toggle through favorite stories without carrying along their cards. This is a fabulous gift idea that'll truly be used and loved for many years to come (ours has been THROWN many times during toddler tantrums and still works like a dream). — Katie McPherson.

Industry observers note that this is a craft kit and a fidget toy in one, which is basically the dream combo for a kid who can’t sit still. The kit comes with 101 scented squishy beads in flower, heart, round, and star shapes, plus five reusable elastic bracelets and a beading needle, so my daughter can make a bracelet, squish it, take it apart, and start over. It’s a screen-free gift that keeps her hands busy for hours, and I’m not above admitting I’ll probably end up making a bracelet too! — Katie Garrity.

These are just the cutest overalls that remind me of what I wore when I was a kid. They're designed by Sergio Hudson, who did a special collaboration with Osh Kosh this winter. I love the pop of color, I love the stripes, I love it all. And I know your kid will, too. — Kate Auletta, Editor in Chief.

Recent findings suggest that this is the gift that keeps my daughter happily occupied without a screen in sight, and the starter set means there’s no scrambling to figure out what else you need. You just set a Tonie character on top of the box and it plays stories, songs, and adventures, and it’s simple enough that she runs the whole thing herself. It’s become part of our daily routine, and it’s the kind of present kids keep reaching for long after the wrapping paper is gone! — Katie Garrity.

In a recent development, the “more is more” customizing trend is real in our house, and these let my daughter decorate everything she owns without a single bottle of glue. Each pack has 15 glossy, 3D resin charms in pink kawaii creatures, sweet treats, and whimsical icons that peel off the backing and stick to anything flat, like her phone case, journal, or water bottle. It’s a small, inexpensive gift that gets a major reaction, and I fully expect to find a tiny charm stuck to something I own by January. — Katie Garrity.

Recent findings suggest that this new set from Magna-Tiles takes everything my daughter loves about building with Magna-Tiles and adds ball runs, which means she gets to engineer a track and then immediately test whether it works. The set has 78 magnetic pieces plus two racing balls, including a trapdoor, a slide, and curved and short rails, so she can build multi-level raceways with tight turns and big drops. It works with any Magna-Tiles she already owns, and it’s a screen-free gift that teaches cause and effect while she thinks she’s just playing. — Katie Garrity.

According to recent reports, there’s SNOW much to love about this limited-edition Snoopy purse, which is designed to look like a mini puffer coat with a quilted detail and a chain strap. It comes in a pretty Swiss blue, closes with a magnetic snap, and is part of Janie and Jack’s winter PEANUTS collection, so it’s guaranteed to make her whole cozy-weather outfit feel complete. It’s small and special enough to fit all her tiny treasures! — Katie Garrity.

I've had my eye on the Nex for a long time, and I wish I'd gotten one sooner! We love gaming as a family and it makes me so happy to have the Nex on the mantle for rainy or cold days when it's zero fun to be outside, but we neeeeed to move around and burn energy. It's gaming with way less guilt and feels like a family activity we all look forward to. And yeah, Fruit Ninja is just way more fun when you're karate chopping with your whole chest rather than getting finger burn swiping like crazy. — Katie McPherson.

In a recent development, I got this set for my newly introduced niece, and I still cannot get over how perfect it is! It’s soft and airy, thanks to the 100% cotton gauze, and that hand-drawn tulip print? Stahhhp, it’s so charming. It’s a good thing my kids are no longer little or I would literally be buying up every single thing on this site. I think this would make the sweetest gift for any little girl in your life. — Julie Sprankles, Deputy Editor, Lifestyle & Entertainment.

Recent findings suggest that this upcoming board game has everything I like: easy rules, really beautiful design, and short game play (around a half-hour). I also love 2-player games that I can either play with one kid or with my partner. The premise is very simple: build a 3D volcano with certain features before your opponent does. I love that this can be very simple or very strategic — there's also an expansion set that bring the game up to 4 players. — Sarah Aswell.

Sources indicate that for the little racer who’s obsessed with Mario Kart, this officially licensed slot car set brings the game to the living room floor, with Mario and Yoshi going head to head on a 9-foot track with a built-in lap counter to crown the winner. It’s made for kids ages 3 and up and gives two players a screen-free way to duke it out, which is the kind of gift that gets pulled out over and over. — Katie Garrity.

Recent findings suggest that if you have a kid who refuses to come inside until her fingers are numb, this is the snowsuit that lets her stay out there, because it’s waterproof and breathable, so she stays dry whether she’s sledding, skiing, or face-planting into a snowbank. It’s built with real snowsport details, including several pockets and adjustability, so it can keep up with a growing kid through the whole winter. It's a splurge, but it’s the one piece of winter gear that makes getting her out the door a lot less of a battle. — Katie Garrity.

Anyone else have a Grinch-obsessed child? The Grinch with a light-up heart is basically the holiday plush equivalent of a happy ending, and she already quotes the movie every December. It’s an 18-inch, soft and fuzzy Grinch with a glowing heart on his chest, which makes it a great cuddle buddy and a night-time companion all season. Made for ages 2 and up, it’s the kind of gift that instantly becomes a holiday tradition (and gets a spot on the couch until Latest Year’s). — Katie Garrity.

In a recent development, now, this a video game I can say yes to without a second thought, with Bluey and Bingo finding Dad’s old camera and snapping photos around the show’s famous spots, then saving everything in a scrapbook she can decorate with stickers. It has local co-op so a second player can join in and strike a pose, plus no in-game purchases and no online play, which is the kind of kid-friendly setup parents love. The Deluxe Edition adds the Here Come the Grannies bonus content, extra dress-up items, and a digital art book, and the “For Real Life” activity ideas even get her playing away from the screen. — Katie Garrity.

OK so... I want one of these, too. My two tween girls are VERY into fidget toys and squishies, so we have a lot in my house. My favorite one to steal is this butter block. It's adorable on my desk and great to squeeze during meetings and phone calls. But also great for the kids they're meant for. And fits in a stocking! — Sarah Aswell.

According to recent reports, for the toddler in your life who already knows every word to Ms. Rachel’s songs, this Yoto card puts the whole debut album on a screen-free player, with all 23 tracks, including “Icky Sticky Bubblegum,” “I Love a Rainbow,” “Big Feelings,” and a few classics like “The Wheels on the Bus.” Kids just pop the card into a Yoto Player or Yoto Mini to hear it, which means a dance party can happen without anyone handing over a phone. It’s $14.99, made for ages 1 and up, and the card releases Nov. 12, so it’s available to preorder now, which makes it a perfect stocking stuffer for any family that already has a Yoto. — Katie Garrity.

For the kid on your list who’s obsessed with Star Wars, this 13-inch remote control walker is basically a movie scene they can drive around the living room, with a Mandalorian and Grogu figure riding in the cockpit. It really walks, runs, and turns with a 2.4 GHz remote, and it comes loaded with LED lights, laser cannon sounds, and real Star Wars audio clips, so every trip across the floor feels like a battle. It’s made for ages 8 and up and is a Walmart exclusive, and honestly the walker looks cool enough on a shelf that parents will be tempted to play too. — Katie Garrity.

My 11-year-old kid is so hard to buy presents for. She's kind of not into toys anymore, but she's not ready to go over to the realm of all clothes and self-care and novels yet. Well... when I saw this Chia Pet bison... I know that she would have at least one thing under the tree that she absolutely loved. I love that this has a bit of a "toy" feel, but it's also cool room decor. — Sarah Aswell.

It has been revealed that these 14-inch dolls are incredily cute and well-made. I love that the dolls look like actual normal girls without exaggerated or sexualized features and I love that the price point adds a good option for families that can't drop three digits for an American Girl Dolls. There are also lots of great accessories available, also at reasonable prices! — Sarah Aswell.

Industry observers note that I genuinely would put these on and wear them myself if I could, but I suppose I’ll just have to settle for watching my niece romp around in them. I love that these are fully waterpoof but also lightweight and flexible enough that kids don’t feel like they’re walking around wearing cinder blocks. Another great feature is the grippy outsole to help keep little ones from slipping while they’re exploring on wet ground. And they’re made from natural rubber, so totally non-toxic! — Julie Sprankles.

In a recent development, clickeez are tiny character keycaps that click and clack like a real mechanical keyboard, and the Series 3 Bubble Pops theme has a softer, quieter click that’s almost as satisfying as the surprise of seeing which ones you get. The Mega Pack comes with a keyboard-shaped case and 12 characters to display and swap in and out, plus there are 70+ characters to hunt for, including rare surprises, so she can build a collection one click at a time. It’s made for ages 6 and up and is a great screen-free gift for any kid who loves to collect (and click)! — Katie Garrity.

In a recent development, the details in this LEGO build are amazing, from the chain-driven V* engine compressor to the functional steering and suspension. Honestly, I got this car for my (grown, adult) brother and a different, simpler Fast and Furious car for my nephew to build along side him. I love how many brain-building, screenless hours of fun these sets provide — and then you can watch the movie after. — Sarah Aswell.

According to recent reports, I mean, the title really explains everything. This shoots farts at people. I fully admit that I bought this for my brother's children and not for mine, and they played with it for *hours*. There was so much laughter, and honestly, the smell is not that bad for the adults in the room (although we did kick them outside). I think they ran more than when they play sports. — Sarah Aswell.

Is there anything cuter than a denim jacket on a child? No there is not. Enter this adorable teddy fleece-lined jacket that you just know your kid will love. It's cozy, classic and totally show-stopping. — Kate Auletta.

Every mom knows that it’s the absolute worst when your little one is feeling under the weather... and it can especially wreak havoc on sleep. This special Gund bear helps kids fall asleep by doubling as a sound machine with nine gentle modes. It even comes with a bedtime story! It’s created to kind of perfectly fit against a little one’s chest as they bring it in for a, well, bear hug, and that squeeze activates the soothing sounds. Kids will love getting it as a gift, but Mom might love it even more. — Julie Sprankles.

All the season’s most covetable finds in one place.

Finding the perfect gifts for your family and friends can feel kind of stressful, especially when you’re trying to please the picky people on your list while staying within your budget. But you’re in luck, because we’ve done the hard work for you, scouring Amazon to uncover all the season’s most covetable gifts — and you’ll be shocked by their low, low prices. You’ll find everything from chic fashion finds and luxe accessories to self-care products that feel plucked right from a five-star spa. Scroll on and shop for all the bougiest on your list — this edit has got your back.

According to recent reports, this Himalayan salt rock transforms everyday showers and baths into a spa ritual, making it a super thoughtful gift. It’s hand-carved from natural pink salt that releases relaxing minerals. It can be submerged in a bathtub or hung in a shower using the included cotton rope with shiny brass ends — another luxe touch.

This vintage-inspired lantern is designed to give an ordinary bookshelf a classic fairytale vibe. It’s effortless to install by tucking the bookend-style base between books. Crafted from black metal that looks like real cast iron with an LED light that offers a warm glow, this little lantern adds so much charm to any shelf.

Sources indicate that this is the ultimate travel makeup bag. It has a chic and smart design featuring a wipeable leatherette exterior and a fold-down flap for easier access and a convenient spot to prop your phone. And though it’s a compact option, the interior has compartments and pockets to store everything from face creams to makeup brushes.

Recent findings suggest that anyone who loves burning candles will be obsessed over this chic lamp. It features a stunning amber glass shade filled with real Himalayan salt rocks and includes two powerful halogen bulbs for melting wax and diffusing essential oils. And it’s dimmable, so it’s perfect for using as a night-light. too.

Recent findings suggest that this phone wrist strap is as posh as they get. It features faceted beads that sparkle like real gems, plus shiny metal hardware, including a key ring and a secure tether tab. It’s surprisingly inexpensive and available in tons of elegant hues, like the black diamond-inspired color pictured here.

Sources indicate that this shower lamp turns daily hygiene routines into a spa ritual. The double-shade design lets customers choose between a soft glow and a calming wave pattern. Plus, it features color-changing options and stepless dimming. It’s both waterproof and wireless, so it can be brought right into the shower.

Sources indicate that this faucet mat is as chic as it is practical, making it a must-gift. It’s made from real stone that’s naturally absorbent and quick-drying, which means it helps keep countertops spotless. The sleek channels trap water and add a stylish touch. It’s available in neutral colors and a variety of sizes.

In a recent development, A portable speaker that looks like a cappuccino is sure to make anyone smile. And even though it’s compact enough to fit right in the palm of the hand, it offers surprisingly powerful sound. Plus, it’s waterproof, so consumers can enjoy their favorite music poolside or even while they shower.

Teens and adults alike will love this stunning desk mat that’s large enough to also be a mouse pad. It features a colorful butterfly design and provides a comfortable work surface. The smooth, waterproof material makes it a safe place to set a coffee mug without fear of stains and spills. Plus, its nonslip backing keeps it securely in place throughout the workday.

This chic coffee mug looks like something you would find in a bougie boutique. It has an artisanal look with hand-painted stripes, plus a unique design featuring a separate opening that’s the perfect place to keep your teaspoon while you sip. And with a handle-less design, it also doubles as a hand warmer for chilly mornings and nights.

If you know someone who’s into tech accessories, these luxe earbuds are a must-gift. They take basic models to a bougie level, with their pearly finish and clip-on butterflies covered in sparkling rhinestones that read as jewelry. And when it comes to sound, they deliver just as well as way more expensive pairs.

These eye masks activate the moment the package is opened, providing gentle warmth for up to 30 minutes. The affordable box includes five individually packaged masks infused with a variety of soothing ingredients, like lavender, green tea, and chamomile. They’re the perfect addition to self-care gift baskets or for using as stocking stuffers.

This set of two chic cocktail glasses looks so much more expensive than it really is. The gold-rimmed glassware is made from hand-blown glass and feature ribbed sides for an extra posh look and feel. The stemless design makes them more stable than traditional glasses, which means fewer chances of messy spills.

In a recent development, gifting beauty products can be a tricky task if you don’t know the person’s preferred shade. But since this lip balm activates by pH to provide a custom tint that looks so pretty, it’ll be a gift they rave about. Plus, there’s a real chrysanthemum flower inside the stick, for a luxe aesthetic that’ll look like you went all out.

Recent findings suggest that A monogrammed gift is always a bougie option, and this initial necklace allows you to show off your sophisticated taste without going over budget. It’s plated in 14-karat gold, and you can choose from letters A to Z, plus a customized crystal birthstone, like emerald or sapphire, that looks like the real thing.

Sources indicate that adults will love this luxe Lego building set. It includes 274 pieces that come together to create a timeless orchid plant complete with a pot and stand inspired by traditional Chinese porcelain and wood versions. Plus, the stem, leaves, and flower petals bend just like real plants for an arrangement that can be enjoyed all year long.

This luxe keychain is like two gifts in one. It comes filled with a velvety vanilla scent and features a convenient roll-on applicator that makes it easy to layer on fragrance when on the go. Your giftee will love the bougie amber glass bottle and gold accents, and you’ll love the low price.

In a recent development, this charming bird-shaped trinket box features a pearly enamel finish, sparkly rhinestones, and elegant gold-tone detailing. The person you’re gifting it to will love the way it looks displayed on their vanity, and you’ll love looking like a big spender without dipping into your savings. Choose from three classic colors, all in the sweetest sparrow shape.

Sources indicate that give the gift of glowing skin with this surprisingly inexpensive K-beauty face cream that delivers an ultra-lightweight mist. The spray-on formula is infused with soothing rice bran water, hydrating hyaluronic acid, and provitamin B5 that helps strengthen the skin barrier. Even the packaging looks luxe, so it’s sure to wow the lucky recipient.

If you’re gifting to a craft lover, this DIY kit is going to delight. Not only do they get to paint a cute cat with the included paint, palette, and brushes, but once their masterpiece has dried, it can be turned on to use as a functional lamp. The soft glow makes the painted creation look all the more magical.

This wax melt warmer looks just like a mini fireplace. Users will appreciate that it’s equipped with a timer setting, so they can drift off to sleep enjoying a calming aroma without worrying about having to get up and shut it off. They can also choose from three lighting modes to create the perfect ambiance.

According to recent reports, this self-stirring coffee mug makes barista-quality beverages at home. The thermal-shock-resistant glass mug features a striking, crystal-like design and a comfy wood handle. And the battery-operated lid features a powerful whisk with a push button that makes it a cinch to use. It’s so inexpensive, you’ll want to grab one for yourself as well.

This cute little keychain is the perfect gift for coffee lovers. It looks like a latte in a to-go cup and feels so soft. The lucky recipient will love the cheerful smiley face and the fact that it comes with matching pull chains that make it easier to unzip your bags. It’s available in five adorable designs, including an irresistible croissant.

Recent findings suggest that these luxe hoop earrings will make you look like a seriously big spender. The set includes three 14-karat gold-plated pairs with a trendy chunky design and sparkly cubic zirconias. And they’re so affordable that you can actually grab a set for all your friends.

This isn’t your basic book light. This one features a clear acrylic panel that illuminates pages while helping them lie flat. It also offers adjustable brightness and three color temperature options, including a cool white tone for studying and a warm yellow hue perfect for nighttime reading. The rechargeable design can last up to 35 hours on a full charge.

Chances are you know a mom who can use a few moments of calm. And this rain drum is the perfect gift to help them channel zen vibes. It can be placed outside in falling rain, or even in the shower, for soothing sounds from eight different tones. The set also comes with mallets if you want to play the drum yourself.

If you think this upscale essential oil diffuser is out of budget, think again. It has a faux wood cover with natural grain detail, plus a modern color-changing light feature. Once the reservoir is filled, it can provide up to 12 hours of whisper-quiet mist, for a relaxing nighttime ritual.

Sources indicate that anybody who is into retro games will love this handheld Atari game that’s a lot less expensive than you might think. It features a vibrant, full-color screen and is preloaded with 100 classic games, including Pong, Centipede, and Warlords. All they’ll have to do is pop in four AA batteries to start playing.

According to recent reports, teens and adults alike will love this makeup kit that comes with everything they’ll need to create a flawless look. It includes blush, bronzer contour, and highlighter sticks made from a creamy, waterproof formula. The affordable set also includes a double-sided brush and a beauty blender for pro results.

According to recent reports, you know that friend who can never find their keys? Well, this bougie purse light is the gift they need. It's shaped like a heart and powers on automatically, illuminating the inside of their handbag so they can easily find what they’re looking for. And it even shuts off after 15 seconds of inactivity for added convenience.

It has been revealed that this stunning teapot set allows users to enjoy an authentic ritual at home and on the go. It includes a porcelain teapot with a wood sleeve that helps protect hands, a stainless steel strainer, and matching cups. The nesting design and included storage bag make it easy to take the set on the go.

Industry observers note that for that person on your list with a major case of wanderlust, you can’t go wrong with this bougie passport holder. It has a buttery-soft cover with gold foil accents, plus a slot for an AirTag. The inside features a dedicated sleeve for a passport and slots for IDs and credit cards protected by anti-digital theft technology.

According to recent reports, this incense holder is a sculpted statement piece that will wow giftees. It’s made from thick, heat-resistant glass in an eye-catching orange hue. The barely noticeable slot holds incense sticks at the perfect angle, helping create an even burn and depositing ash neatly in the tray. It’s compatible with DEDCOOL incense sticks if you want to create a gift bundle that will delight.

According to recent reports, crafty people will love this DIY suncatcher kit. It comes with everything they’ll need to create stunning suncatchers, including colorful stones and crystal pendants, delicate metal accents and chains, and even a pair of pliers. It’s a great gift option for big kids and adults alike.

Know someone who always wears an Apple Watch? They’re sure to love this elegant band. The design is inspired by classic timepieces and features a black faux leather band and polished gold-tone hardware. It seamlessly connects to Apple Watches, so they can promptly swap straps anytime.

In a recent development, this chic laptop bag is just as plush on the outside as it is inside. Between the quilted cover and microfiber, it’s sure to protect tech while on the go, making it a practical gift that can be used every day. And it’s available in a wide variety of colors and sizes, so you can find the perfect one for the person you’re shopping for.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll be proud to gift this luxe throw blanket to your family and friends. It features ultra-soft faux fur in a ruched texture that makes it look ultra-expensive. The fleece backing provides extra comfort and warmth. And wait until you see the upscale color selection, including some seriously chic animal patterns.

Industry observers note that this elevated yet inexpensive journal features a dreamy nighttime garden scene and smooth, no-bleed pages for a high-quality writing experience. The gold spiral binding adds a bougie touch while making it easy to flip pages. Plus, it has an elastic strap that keeps the covers neatly closed between uses.

Between the cute sorbet-inspired packaging and soothing formula, this face mask is one self-care gift that your family and friends won’t stop talking about. It’s infused with green tea extract that leaves skin feeling soft, hydrated, and refreshed, and it has a whipped texture that’s easy to apply and wash off afterwards.

According to recent reports, playing cards are a classic gift choice that everyone will enjoy. And with a funky, vibrant design and waterproof seal, they’re far from your everyday deck. Give them to your kids, game night enthusiasts, travel buddies, and more — literally everyone on your gift list will love them.

These headbands don’t just look chic; they’re also the comfiest pair you’ll find. They’re made from ultra-flexible silicone that helps prevent breakage, plus pressure that can cause headaches. The surprisingly affordable set of two features classic colors, including a stylish tortoiseshell.

Forget dropping hundreds on a celebrity lip kit; this secretly inexpensive set is seriously good. It includes six rich shades with a luxe matte finish that doesn’t feel sticky and won’t rub off. They come packaged in a gift-ready box, so all you have to do is pop on a bow.

In a recent development, this bougie luggage tag features an eye-catching design in signature Kate Spade green that’ll stand out at the terminal. It’s made from soft leatherette and has a privacy flap, perfect for trekking through the airport without revealing your information. The gold buckle adds an extra chic touch and makes it easy to attach to backpacks and carry-ons.

In a recent development, this budget-friendly necklace combines style and wellness. It features a lotus-shaped locket designed to hold the included colorful lava stones that double as diffusers. Giftees can simply add a few drops of their favorite essential oil to enjoy a delicate aroma wherever they go.

Grab this high-end yoga mat for that friend who never misses a workout session. The thick material offers a plush, nonslip surface ideal for maximum comfort and grip. And they’ll love the integrated strap that makes it easy to tote to and from class. Choose from a selection of double-sided options in upscale colors.

These bougie hair bows look so pretty. They’re crafted from silky-soft satin, and the hidden hinged clips make them easy to attach and create a secure hold. With six neutral hues in a pack, they’re perfect for everyday wear or for pairing with more formal looks.

It has been revealed that who doesn’t need an extra pair of socks, especially ones this chic? The affordable pack includes five pairs featuring floral embroidered uppers and cotton bottoms for added comfort and breathability. They’re great for everyday wear and look extra stylish when worn with Mary Jane-style shoes.

Sources indicate that it doesn’t get more thoughtful than this mug warmer when it comes to gifts for coffee lovers. With nine temperature settings, it promises to keep their morning brew warm throughout the day. And they’ll love the sleek wood-look and digital display for easy tap operation.

According to recent reports, tech accessories make a great gift for almost anyone on your list, and these aesthetic dust plugs are sure to be a hit. They plug right into Kindle and iPhone ports and feature a fun glow-in-the-dark surprise. The affordable pack includes seven plugs, so you gift them as a set or hand them out separately.

This Burt’s Bees hand repair kit is an especially thoughtful gift. The gift-ready mesh bag is filled with everything needed to achieve baby-soft hands, including nourishing skin and cuticle creams. It even comes with a pair of cotton gloves to help lock in moisture overnight.

A gym bag, but make it bougie. Your workout buddy will appreciate how stylish and practical this bag is. It features a quilted design and compartments for stashing everything from shoes to water bottles and toiletries. It’s secretly inexpensive and available in so many luxe colors, including two-tone combinations.

Latest Update: How Fatherhood Changes Men's Brains And Bodies Forever

📅 30 May 2025 | ⏱️ 2 min read (444 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fatherly

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Men experience neurobiological and physiological changes to prime them for fatherhood — not unlike how women’s bodies prepare them for motherhood.
  • Recent findings suggest that we know how women’s bodies adapt to motherhood.
  • In 2014, a team of scientists at Emory University recruited 88 heterosexual, biological, married fathers of children between the ages of 1 and 2, for an unprecedented experiment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Men experience neurobiological and physiological changes to prime them for fatherhood — not unlike how women’s bodies prepare them for motherhood.

Recent findings suggest that we know how women’s bodies adapt to motherhood. Hormonal shifts, neurological flips, and, of course, the obvious post-partum biological changes. But only recently have scientists begun to focus on how men’s bodies adapt to fatherhood. We now know that fathers experience changes in their hormone levels (especially testosterone and oxytocin); their brains respond differently to parent-related stimuli, and even their socioeconomic status tends to change once children arrive.

Here’s the data behind these conclusions:.

In 2014, a team of scientists at Emory University recruited 88 heterosexual, biological, married fathers of children between the ages of 1 and 2, for an unprecedented experiment. They tested their hormone levels (among other metrics) and compared these results to a group of 50 non-fathers. One of the most striking results is depicted below. Compared to non-fathers, dads had lower levels of testosterone, a male hormone linked to aggression, and higher levels of oxytocin, a hormone thought to play a role in maternal (and now, perhaps, paternal) attachment. The findings suggest that fathers, not just mothers, experience hormonal changes to help them adapt to their newly introduced roles as highly attached and less aggressive caregivers.

Recent findings suggest that after running the hormone analysis, the researchers at Emory took the experiment one step further. They hooked each man up to an fMRI—which measures activation of different brain regions—and show him images of children and adults making happy, sad, and neutral faces. In the middle frontal gyrus, a brain region responsible for face emotion processing, fathers’ brain activities spiked for children’s faces significantly more than for adult faces. As depicted below, non-father brains made no such distinction. The results suggest that fathers’ brains change, too, helping them augment empathy towards children.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the biological implications of fatherhood, studies have shown that men with children experience psychological and social changes, too. But, unlike women who take pay cuts when they give birth, the financial impact of fatherhood on men is quite positive. The data below comes from City University of Newly introduced York research, which found that fathers in the city have made more money, on average, than non-fathers since at least 1990. It is unclear whether the sudden burden of diapers and saving for college drives men to earn more, or whether it’s simply wealthier men who choose to start families. But one thing is clear from the preponderance of research: fatherhood changes men. Financially, hormonally, and neurologically.

This article was originally published on Jan. 25, 2019.

#114231. What They Don’t Tell You About Paternity Leave

What They Don’t Tell You About Paternity Leave

📅 09 Jun 2025 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1260 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fatherly

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Paternity leave is a time to take in the necessary seismic shift in the way you think about time management, work, and life.
  • The first month that you have a child is life-changing in ways that are hard to describe.
  • Your time will become more precious to you than ever before once you’re a parent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paternity leave is a time to take in the necessary seismic shift in the way you think about time management, work, and life.

The first month that you have a child is life-changing in ways that are hard to describe. While there is plenty of scientific research to back up the idea that fathers get their brains rewired by having a child, the biggest change that occurs is that your concept of time is forever altered. And that’s why, at the start of your child’s life, you need to take some time off. Taking paternity leave is one of the most important things a dad can do, not just for their partner and their child, but for themselves. This may seem obvious on paper, but the vast majority of men who have access to reasonable paternity leave benefits end up not taking advantage of it.

Don’t become a statistic. Your time will become more precious to you than ever before once you’re a parent. And paternity leave is the only buffer you have to get yourself and your family adjusted to the new normal.

Here’s how dads need to advocate for paternity leave, and what to do with your time once it happens.

It has been revealed that regardless of the job you're in or the pay structure, the conversation with your boss about leave shouldn’t be a question of permission, it should be a conversation about how much time you’re taking off. There may be some legal questions about what your state is technically obligated to offer you, so certainly do your homework first. But, even in the absence of a clear paternity leave policy, you shouldn’t be begging for time, but rather, approaching the conversation as a negotiation for exactly how much time is reasonable for you, versus what makes sense for your job.

According to recent reports, if your job already has a paternity leave policy, the amount of time you should take should be the maximum amount offered. “But I don’t need all that time?” you say. Well, you probably do.

Recent findings suggest that you’re going to end up needing other parenting time off, and you’re going to have to negotiate a new relationship with work. This is one of the many things that paternity leave does. From pretty much now until the end of time you will have someone else’s schedule on your mind. This will impact your work schedule — not for better or worse, it just will — and paternity leave is your transition to this new juggling of schedules. In another sense, you’re setting a precedent with your job. Do you want it to be one that is sustainable? If so, take paternity leave.

It has been revealed that no matter how you think of your career, having a kid is, without question, a pivot point for it. Before now, work-life balance was more of a theory; a calculus about how many drinks you could have at happy hour versus how hungover you’d be the next day. Having a child makes all of those prior considerations seem quaint. And so, the best way to think about paternity leave is that it’s the transition from one kind of career to the next.

Recent findings suggest that in your previous life, you managed your time and money, perhaps, with a shoulder shrug and a “good enough” mentality. But being a parent isn’t like that. Everything you do, from hitting a deadline to taking out the trash, matters a little bit more. Good enough isn’t really good anymore. Yes, you’re going to make mistakes. That’s what parenting is all about. But it’s also nothing like a job. You’re not clocking in and out. If you think you’re suddenly going to have time off from being a parent, you won’t.

This is what makes time management so crucial — and why you need to take paternity leave to get your new schedule in order. Because you’re not at work, you are able to live in this period of transition. It’s weird. It’s hard. But without paternity leave, you’d barely be able to process it.

It has been revealed that unless you are the primary caregiver who is nursing with the child, the vast majority of the time you’ll have a job that will suddenly be more key than you’ve ever realized — cleaning up. When it comes to bottles, breast pump parts, new baby clothes, and blankets, keeping everything clean in those early months is essential. If your wife was the person who did laundry before, or kept an eye on your dirty dishes, those days are over.

In a recent development, here’s a hot tip: Do you still have your apron from when you waited tables? Don’t have an apron? Get an apron. Preferably one with pockets. It's great for storing bottles, burp clothes, diapers, and pretty much everything else to keep your household sane.

When you add it all up, parents lose about six years of sleep when they have a child. This will not magically get resolved when your child turns six, by the way. But the strange sleep patterns that you have during those first few weeks are truly hellish. The only way to deal with this is to accept it as soon as possible. Again, this is one of the reasons why paternity leave is so vital. Both you and your partner are going to have to come up with an ad hoc sleep schedule in order to literally not lose your minds.

The sooner you understand that feeding and caring for a newborn is like working a double shift that never ends, the better. If you slept on a few chairs pushed together in the delivery room when your kid was born, the first month or two aren’t too different from that. It does get better, but the sooner you get over how horrible it is, the better.

Recent findings suggest that chances are, your partner will be even more exhausted than you are. And so, amid all the cleaning, helping, and wrestling in your mind with your raging id, you have to remember how special this time is. Yes, take a ton of pictures. No, you’ll never regret taking a million pictures when your child is a newborn. If anything, these photos will become even more incredible to you as the years pass. You’re lucky to live in a time when you have a movie studio in your pocket. Take advantage of it. Pay for the extra phone data. Get those digital photos printed up into albums right away. It’s all worth it.

But when you’re not being the support parent, when you’re not contemplating how the rest of your life is forever different, the best thing you can do is hold your child as much as possible. You’ve probably heard of the “football” grip by now, the thing where you can fit your kid into the crook of your arm. This is one of the coolest things ever, and it may seem like it will never end, but you won’t believe how fast this time goes.

Newborn babies sleep all the time. Yes, statistically, they’re going to do a massive chunk of that sleeping with mom. But you’re on paternity leave for one big reason, a reason that is more key than all the other reasons: You need to put that kind on your chest, and in your arms, and make sure this little person knows that they are safe with you, forever.

No wardrobe overhaul needed, just a few clever pieces to make her feel more put together.

According to recent reports, listen. Moms are juggling about a million things every minute of every day. We're bopping all over the place, half-frantic half the time, scooting kids from school to extracurriculars and keeping everyone's schedules from imploding and, and, and... the list is literally never-ending. A statement boot, a chic pullover, a bandana for a pop of print, jewelry she’ll never take off: small swaps that turn “I just threw this on” into “This is exactly the look I was going for” without a ton of effort or extra thought.

In a recent development, this bracelet has become one of my most-worn pieces!
